reason: Response 1 handles the access-control core with useful depth (session isolation, existence-confirming refusals, side channels), but Response 2 covers the wider harm set (hallucination, over-reliance, disclosure, log retention) with a per-harm test table that has controls, owner-set thresholds and stop conditions, sizes probes statistically, routes employee-privacy and privilege questions to counsel, and gives a dated, owned plan.
